newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra says can set conditions for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra says can set conditions for rate cut.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday the government could set up the conditions for an easing in interest rates.

"In a low inflation economy where we have the opportunity for wages based on productivity outcomes, where we have co-operation both at the executive and non-executive level, we can set up the conditions for an easing in relation to the high interest rates which were the legacy of the failed Keating years," Costello told parliament.
Costello was responding to a question from his own backbench.
Australia's Liberal-National government, which ousted former prime minister Paul Keating's Labor government in March, has blamed Labor for Australia's relatively high interest rates.
The central bank, the Reserve Bank, in July cut official cash rates to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent, the first rate cut in three years.

Costello earlier on Tuesday told a meeting of members of the Liberal and National parties that following price data released last week commentators saw conditions favourable for the prospect of lower interest rates, a Liberal spokesman told reporters.
